correctness.rationale: Smooth Birkhoff orthogonality in \(\ell_3^2\) gives a complete one-parameter tangent family. After including both tangent orientations, the cubic rectangular ratio becomes \(F(t,s)\). Three sign regions are eliminated by explicit positive denominator-minus-numerator factorizations. On the only region capable of exceeding one, the change \(u=t^3\) and \(h=st^2\) gives the rational function \(R(u,h)\). Its finite boundary is below one and all escaping paths tend to one. The exact derivative resultant has one admissible root \(u\ge1\); the linear subresultant forces a unique \(h\in(4,5)\), and substitution is certified modulo \(P\). Hence the unique interior point is the global maximizer.
risks: The algebraic maximum is represented by an isolated degree-ten root rather than radicals.
The arbitrary-dimensional value \(\mu_3(\ell_3)\) is not claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly notes that exact generalized rectangular constants are generally unknown and supplies only broad \(\ell_p\) estimates. The result closes the first untreated smooth cubic planar case after the indexed quartic computation, identifies a unique nontrivial interior Birkhoff orbit, and supplies a reusable exact resultant/Sturm method for smooth non-Hilbert planes. This is a natural invariant/object pairing rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
risks: The result is a sharp planar benchmark, not a full exponent or dimension theorem.
